newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ORIENTAL DAILY -- Beijing wants a sum of money in the 1997/98 Hong Kong budget for establishing the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government. But decisions have not been reached over whether the Hong Kong Government should pay the costs of the provisional legislature before the handover.
-- A Canadian Hong Kong Chinese was beaten up when going through the Shenzhen immigration post because he could not write in Chinese and he filled in a form in English.
-- MING PAO -- Research by the Hong Kong Youth Association showed the Diaoyu Islands protest had raised the sense of nationality of young people in Hong Kong.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- The fifth meeting of the Preparatory Committee adopted guidelines on how to select Hong Kong's first chief executive.
-- Chinese experts estimate China's economy will grow rapidly and steadily during the ninth five year plan period.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Property developer Chi Cheung Investment said it would buy in property agency Ricacorp Properties.
-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Cafe-bakery chain Delifrance will consolidate its lucrative niche in Asia by going public through a listing on the Singapore exchange.

-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- Beijing is mulling over banning foreign firms from holding controlling stakes in some industrial joint ventures, accusing them of exploiting China's markets without considering the interests of their Chinese partners.
-- Footwear maker and retailer Le Saunda Holdings plans to invest $12 million to set up its fourth production line, for men's footwear, in China early next year.
